summary: Mainstream pack hype was all Pokémon TCG Pocket today: the Dual Fusion set landed on 28 Oct and reveal posts pulled tens of thousands of views. On the crypto side, a small analyst account put Collector Crypt at $19.16M revenue in 30 days, far ahead of Courtyard at $2.23M, and a new Solana app, JustPlayTCG, teased graded-card packs with Google, X or email sign-in and 'no crypto know-how needed'. Jupiter kept pushing its Gacha with a TCG trivia night, and PrizePicks Packs users complained about bad pulls and missing bonus packs. Solflare Packs talk was steady and positive, but almost all from small ambassador-style accounts with low views.

sources_note: X search via the x connector, posts from 2026-10-27 09:00 UTC to 2026-10-28 09:00 UTC, 8 searches. Engagement numbers are copied from the X API at scan time. Collector Crypt revenue figures and the Pump.fun pack return figures are third-party claims, not confirmed by the companies. Raflux funding comes from a third-party post. Payments talk was thin: the only relevant signal was JustPlayTCG's Google/X/email sign-in pitch; card, Apple Pay and Google Pay searches returned mostly spam. Most Solflare Packs posts come from small ambassador-style accounts with low impressions, so read them as campaign activity, not organic demand. The Turbo mode idea is marked for legal check because auto-sell touches buyback terms. Spam, restock bots, giveaway farms, token shills and carding posts were skipped. Creators already in collector-base.csv or in earlier daily files were excluded.
